notes: Second repo for the eval, chosen to be structurally different from psf/requests: a decorator-heavy CLI framework with a deep class hierarchy (Command/Group/Parameter/ParamType), versus requests' flatter, function-call-heavy HTTP client. Same process as the requests set: every answer was written by reading src/click directly at the pinned commit and confirming it against the source, not by running either system. Same accept_any convention: a question answerable either by the call site or by the callee's own definition gets both locations and accept_any=true; an enumeration question lists every location and every one counts.

questions.question: Which classes inherit directly from UsageError?
questions.answer: Six classes list UsageError as a direct base, all in src/click/exceptions.py: BadParameter, NoSuchOption, NoSuchCommand, BadOptionUsage, BadArgumentUsage and NoArgsIsHelpError.
questions.notes: MissingParameter inherits from BadParameter, not directly from UsageError, so it is deliberately excluded.

questions.question: Which classes inherit directly from ClickException?
questions.answer: Two classes: UsageError and FileError.

questions.question: What class does Group inherit from?
questions.answer: Group inherits from Command.
questions.notes: A single-answer check, not an enumeration — tests whether a system states this correctly rather than guessing a sibling class or Command's own base.

questions.question: What does Context.exit do before it raises an exception?
questions.answer: It calls self.close() to run any registered cleanup callbacks and context managers, then raises Exit(code).
questions.notes: Evidenced equally by exit's own body (819) or close's definition (689).

questions.question: What calls Context.exit?
questions.answer: Command.main calls ctx.exit() after invoking the command in standalone mode (core.py:1562). It is also called from the callbacks of three eager options: version_option, custom_version_option and help_option in decorators.py.

questions.question: Which classes inherit directly from Parameter?
questions.answer: Two classes: Option and Argument.

questions.question: Which class inherits directly from IntParamType?
questions.answer: IntRange.
questions.notes: A one-answer trap similar in shape to a plain inheritance check: an ungrounded system can plausibly guess a different numeric type instead of checking.

questions.question: What does UsageError.show call to write the error message out?
questions.answer: It calls echo(), writing the usage string, an optional "try --help" hint, and the error message to stderr.

questions.question: Where is the function that returns the currently active click context defined, and what does it do if there isn't one?
questions.answer: get_current_context, in src/click/globals.py. It reads the top of a thread-local stack; if the stack is empty it raises RuntimeError ("There is no active click context"), unless called with silent=True, in which case it returns None.
questions.notes: Needs a name discovered first — the question describes behaviour, not an identifier. Lines 13 and 17 are @overload stubs for the same name; 20 is the real implementation.

questions.question: What decorator makes a callback receive the current Context as its first argument, and how does it get hold of that context?
questions.answer: pass_context. It wraps the function so that when called, it looks up the context itself via get_current_context() and passes it as the first argument, rather than the caller passing it explicitly.

questions.question: What method does a parameter type call to reject an invalid value, and what exception does it raise?
questions.answer: ParamType.fail. It raises BadParameter with the given message.

questions.question: What method builds a command's full --help text, and what does it call to do the writing?
questions.answer: Command.get_help builds and returns the help text as a string. It does so by creating a formatter and calling self.format_help(ctx, formatter), which in turn calls format_usage, format_help_text, format_arguments, format_options and format_epilog in sequence.

questions.question: What decorator turns a function into a Command, and what does it use as the command's help text if none is given explicitly?
questions.answer: The command decorator (src/click/decorators.py). If no help text is passed in attrs, it falls back to the decorated function's own docstring (f.__doc__).
questions.notes: Lines 138, 144, 153 and 163 are @overload stubs for the same name; 168 is the real implementation.

questions.question: What tracks where a parameter's value came from — the command line, an environment variable, a default, or a prompt — and where is it defined?
questions.answer: ParameterSource, an IntEnum defined in src/click/core.py with members PROMPT, COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT, DEFAULT_MAP and DEFAULT, ordered from most to least explicit so they can be compared.

questions.question: How does click decide the process exit code when a ClickException reaches the top level unhandled?
questions.answer: Each exception class carries its own exit_code class attribute. ClickException itself defaults to 1; UsageError overrides it to 2, so a usage error and a generic failure exit with different codes.

questions.question: How does click report a usage error, like an unrecognised option, to the user?
questions.answer: UsageError.show prints the command's usage line, a hint suggesting --help (when a help option exists), and an "Error: ..." line with the message, all written to stderr.

questions.question: How can a helper function access the current click context without it being passed in explicitly?
questions.answer: By calling get_current_context(), which reads a thread-local stack that click pushes onto when a context is entered — an implicit alternative to the pass_context decorator.

questions.question: What happens when a required option or argument is missing from the input?
questions.answer: Parameter.process_value checks whether the value is missing after type casting; if the parameter is required and the value is missing, it raises MissingParameter.

questions.question: How does click order the possible sources of a parameter's value, from most to least explicit?
questions.answer: PROMPT, then COMMANDLINE, then ENVIRONMENT, then DEFAULT_MAP, then DEFAULT — the ParameterSource enum members are ordered so a lower value means a more explicit source, and can be compared directly.

questions.question: How does click derive a command's name automatically from its function name when @click.command() is used without an explicit name?
questions.answer: It lowercases the function name and replaces underscores with dashes, then strips a trailing -command, -cmd, -group or -grp suffix — for example init_data_command becomes init-data.

questions.question: How does a Choice parameter type validate that an input value is one of the allowed choices?
questions.answer: Choice.convert normalizes the input value and looks for a matching entry in its normalized choice mapping; if none matches, it calls self.fail with an invalid-choice message, which raises BadParameter.

questions.question: What does Command.main do differently when standalone_mode is False instead of the default True?
questions.answer: In standalone mode, a ClickException is shown and the process exits via sys.exit with its exit code, and an Exit exception also calls sys.exit. With standalone_mode=False, a ClickException is re-raised instead of being printed and exiting, and an Exit's code is returned from the call instead of terminating the process — main() is then usable as a library call rather than a program entry point.
